children: Basis bids for corn and soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf were mixed on Thursday, as traders and brokers closely tracked a storm heading toward the Gulf Coast.
Empty barge prices on interior rivers ticked lower on Thursday, though some spots along the Illinois River did trade higher for nearby availability, brokers said.
One trader said some buyers were eager to get grain and barges moved ahead of Hurricane Isaias, which is gaining strength and approaching the northern Gulf Coast, meteorologists said.

CIF soybean barges loaded in the last-half of October traded at 94 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures. Barges loaded in November also traded at 108 cents, 110 cents and 111 cents over November futures.
Meanwhile, CIF soybean barges loaded in October were bid at 86 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, while November barge loadings firmed and were bid at 109 cents over futures.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybean shipments in October held steady at around 110 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, while November were offered at 117 cents over futures.

Meanwhile, CIF corn barges loaded in October were bid at 70 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, easing from Wednesday, while corn barges loaded in November were bid at 84 cents over December futures.

FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first-half of October were steady at around 97 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, while vessels loaded in last-half October were offered at 95 cents over December futures.
The Taiwan Flour Millers' Association purchased an estimated 105,800 metric tons of milling wheat to be sourced from the United States in a tender on Wednesday, European traders said on Thursday.
The US Department of Agriculture reported export sales of US corn at 769,500 metric tons for the week ended October 1, in line with trade expectations for 600,000 to 1,700,000 tons.
USDA also reported export sales of US soybeans at 549,400 metric tons in the week ended October 1, toward the low end of trade expectations for 450,000 to 1,200,000 tons.
Analysts surveyed by Reuters on average expect the USDA to leave its estimate of the national 2026 soybean yield unchanged from last month at 52.8 bushels per acre on Friday.

US corn and soybean futures eased on Thursday on active harvesting around the Midwest and as investors squared positions ahead of a monthly US government supply and demand report due on Friday. (GRA/)
